وَيَنْبَغِي أَنْ يُشَارِكَ المُجْتَمَعُ فِي صَوْنِ تُرَاثِهِ
وَلَوْ كَانَتْ سِيَاسَاتُ الحِفَاظِ أَصْرَمَ، لَكَانَتِ المَوَاقِعُ أَفْضَلَ حَالًا
وَلَوْ أُولِيَ التُّرَاثُ اهْتِمَامًا كَافِيًا، لَمَا انْدَثَرَ الكَثِيرُ
وَإِذَا اعْتَمَدْنَا سِيَاسَاتِ حِمَايَةٍ صَارِمَةً سَنَضْمَنُ بَقَاءَهُ
live_builder.feedback: Each past-perfect achievement, requirement and regret is accurate on its own, so any three different combinations work.

builder_tasks.title: Use the past perfect for the ancestors
builder_tasks.instruction: Repair the tense for what earlier generations had built.
builder_tasks.source: بَنَتِ الأَجْيَالُ السَّابِقَةُ هٰذِهِ المَعَالِمَ قَبْلَ قُرُونٍ.
options: كَانَتِ الأَجْيَالُ السَّابِقَةُ قَدْ بَنَتْ هٰذِهِ المَعَالِمَ.
تَبْنِي الأَجْيَالُ السَّابِقَةُ هٰذِهِ المَعَالِمَ الآنَ.
builder_tasks.feedback: An achievement completed before the argument takes the past perfect كَانَ قَدْ.

builder_tasks.title: Fix the necessity subjunctive
builder_tasks.instruction: Repair the verb after مِنَ الضَّرُورِيِّ أَنْ.
builder_tasks.source: مِنَ الضَّرُورِيِّ أَنْ يُرَمِّمُ المُتَخَصِّصُونَ المَوَاقِعَ.
options: مِنَ الضَّرُورِيِّ أَنْ يُرَمِّمَ المُتَخَصِّصُونَ المَوَاقِعَ.
مِنَ الضَّرُورِيِّ أَنْ يُرَمِّمْ المُتَخَصِّصُونَ المَوَاقِعَ.
مِنَ الضَّرُورِيِّ أَنْ رَمَّمَ المُتَخَصِّصُونَ المَوَاقِعَ.
builder_tasks.feedback: مِنَ الضَّرُورِيِّ أَنْ takes a subjunctive: يُرَمِّمَ.

builder_tasks.title: Fix the object of يَصُونُ
builder_tasks.instruction: Repair the complement after يَصُونُ.
builder_tasks.source: تَصُونُ السِّيَاسَاتُ الحَكِيمَةُ بِالهُوِيَّةِ.
builder_tasks.feedback: يَصُونُ takes a direct object.

lessons.title: Reading — Built and Natural World Texts
lessons.summary: Read environmental and heritage texts closely (R1–R4), identify the subjunctive triggers — purpose, volition, necessity — and choose subjunctive versus indicative in a gap.
objectives: Answer R1–R4 comprehension questions on built/natural world texts.
Identify a subjunctive verb by its final fatḥa and name its trigger.
Explain what the trigger reveals about the writer's argument (R3).
Choose subjunctive or indicative in a gap-fill by spotting the trigger.
success: I locate the exact phrase that proves each answer.
I classify a subjunctive as purpose (لِكَي), volition or necessity.
I read a necessity trigger as “required but not yet done”.
I put the subjunctive fatḥa only after a trigger, the indicative elsewhere.

teach.title: The subjunctive signals what is not yet done
teach.text: A verb with a final fatḥa after a trigger describes an action that is desired, required or aimed at — not yet happening. يَتَطَلَّبُ أَنْ يُطَوِّرَ says “it requires development” (not done); لِكَي يُطَوِّرَ says “in order to develop” (the goal). Reading which trigger is used reveals the writer's argument.

teach.title: In a gap-fill, find the trigger first
teach.text: If a gap follows لِكَي / يَتَطَلَّبُ أَنْ / يَنْبَغِي أَنْ / يَهْدِفُ إِلَى أَنْ, the answer is subjunctive (fatḥa). If there is no such trigger, the verb is indicative (ḍamma). Spot the trigger, then choose the ending.

grammar.title: Reading subjunctives for argument
grammar.overview: A reading toolkit: identify the subjunctive by its fatḥa, name its trigger type, read its argumentative force, and choose subjunctive versus indicative in a gap.

rules.heading: Identify by the fatḥa
rules.explanation: A trigger + a verb ending in fatḥa is a subjunctive.

rules.heading: Name the trigger
rules.explanation: لِكَي = purpose; يَتَطَلَّبُ / يَهْدِفُ = volition; يَنْبَغِي = necessity.

rules.heading: Read the force (R3)
rules.explanation: The subjunctive marks a desired or required action, hinting at what is lacking.
examples: يَتَطَلَّبُ أَنْ … → the writer says this is necessary but undone

rules.heading: Gap-fill choice
rules.explanation: Spot the trigger, then pick the ending.

quiz.prompt: Which verb is subjunctive?
quiz.feedback: After أَنْ the verb ends in a fatḥa: تُطَوِّرَ.

quiz.prompt: What triggers the subjunctive in «لِكَيْ تُقَلِّلَ الهَدْرَ»?
quiz.feedback: لِكَيْ is the purpose trigger.

quiz.prompt: What triggers it in «يَتَطَلَّبُ الوَضْعُ أَنْ تَتَعَاوَنَ»?
quiz.feedback: يَتَطَلَّبُ أَنْ is a volition trigger.

quiz.prompt: What triggers it in «يَنْبَغِي أَنْ تُطَوِّرَ»?
quiz.feedback: يَنْبَغِي أَنْ is a necessity trigger.

quiz.prompt: What does a necessity subjunctive tell you (R3)?
options: The action is required but not yet done
quiz.feedback: A necessity subjunctive marks a required, undone action.

quiz.prompt: Gap-fill: يَنْبَغِي أَنْ ___ الدُّوَلُ التَّحْلِيَةَ.
quiz.feedback: A trigger requires the subjunctive fatḥa.

quiz.prompt: Gap-fill (no trigger): ___ الدُّوَلُ سِيَاسَاتِهَا حَالِيًّا.
quiz.feedback: With no trigger, the verb is indicative: تُطَوِّرُ.

listening.title: Listening: reading grammar for meaning
listening.script: عِنْدَمَا تَقْرَأُ نَصًّا بِيئِيًّا أَوْ تُرَاثِيًّا، لَا تَنْظُرْ إِلَى المَعْلُومَةِ فَقَطْ، بَلْ إِلَى صِيغَةِ الفِعْلِ. فَالفِعْلُ المَنْصُوبُ يَنْتَهِي بِفَتْحَةٍ، وَيَأْتِي بَعْدَ مُحَفِّزٍ: «لِكَيْ» لِلْغَرَضِ، وَ«يَتَطَلَّبُ أَنْ» لِلْإِرَادَةِ، وَ«يَنْبَغِي أَنْ» لِلضَّرُورَةِ. وَهٰذَا يُخْبِرُكَ بِعَلَاقَةِ الكَاتِبِ بِالفِعْلِ: هَلْ يَصِفُ غَرَضًا، أَمْ يُعَبِّرُ عَنْ حَاجَةٍ، أَمْ يُقَرِّرُ ضَرُورَةً؟ فَالمَنْصُوبُ يَدُلُّ عَلَى أَنَّ الفِعْلَ مَطْلُوبٌ وَلٰكِنْ لَمْ يَحْدُثْ بَعْدُ. أَمَّا الفِعْلُ المَرْفُوعُ فَيَنْتَهِي بِضَمَّةٍ وَيَصِفُ فِعْلًا وَاقِعًا. وَفِي مِلْءِ الفَرَاغِ، ابْحَثْ عَنِ المُحَفِّزِ أَوَّلًا، ثُمَّ اخْتَرِ العَلَامَةَ.

reading.title: Reading: a water-policy opinion
reading.text: يَرَى الكَاتِبُ أَنَّ أَزْمَةَ المِيَاهِ فِي العَالَمِ العَرَبِيِّ أَخْطَرُ مِمَّا يَظُنُّ كَثِيرُونَ. فَالمِنْطَقَةُ تَسْتَنْفِدُ مِيَاهَهَا الجَوْفِيَّةَ بِسُرْعَةٍ. يَتَطَلَّبُ الوَضْعُ أَنْ تَتَعَاوَنَ الدُّوَلُ فِي إِدَارَةِ المَوَارِدِ المُشْتَرَكَةِ، وَمِنَ الضَّرُورِيِّ أَنْ تَسْتَثْمِرَ الحُكُومَاتُ فِي التَّحْلِيَةِ. وَتَعْتَمِدُ بَعْضُ الدُّوَلِ الرِّيَّ الحَدِيثَ لِكَيْ تُقَلِّلَ الهَدْرَ. غَيْرَ أَنَّ هٰذِهِ الجُهُودَ مَا زَالَتْ مَحْدُودَةً. لَوْ أُدِيرَتِ المَوَارِدُ بِحِكْمَةٍ مُنْذُ عُقُودٍ، لَمَا وَصَلَتِ المِنْطَقَةُ إِلَى هٰذِهِ النَّدْرَةِ. وَالغَرَضُ مِنَ النَّصِّ إِقْنَاعُ القَارِئِ بِأَنَّ الإِصْلَاحَ ضَرُورِيٌّ وَعَاجِلٌ.

questions.prompt: R1 — What is the writer's main view?
options: The water crisis is more serious than many think
questions.feedback: أَزْمَةَ المِيَاهِ … أَخْطَرُ مِمَّا يَظُنُّ كَثِيرُونَ.

questions.prompt: R2 — What does يَسْتَنْفِدُ mean here?
questions.feedback: تَسْتَنْفِدُ مِيَاهَهَا الجَوْفِيَّةَ بِسُرْعَةٍ — it depletes them.

questions.prompt: R3 — Identify a volition subjunctive and its trigger.
options: يَتَطَلَّبُ الوَضْعُ أَنْ تَتَعَاوَنَ — trigger يَتَطَلَّبُ
questions.feedback: يَتَطَلَّبُ أَنْ is a volition trigger; تَتَعَاوَنَ is subjunctive.

questions.prompt: R3 — What does the necessity subjunctive «مِنَ الضَّرُورِيِّ أَنْ تَسْتَثْمِرَ» reveal?
options: Investment is required but not yet done — the writer urges reform
questions.feedback: A necessity subjunctive marks a required, undone action.

questions.prompt: R4 — What is the purpose of the text?
options: To persuade the reader that reform is necessary and urgent
questions.feedback: الغَرَضُ مِنَ النَّصِّ إِقْنَاعُ القَارِئِ بِأَنَّ الإِصْلَاحَ ضَرُورِيٌّ وَعَاجِلٌ.

prompts: أَيُّ فِعْلٍ فِي الجُمْلَةِ مَنْصُوبٌ؟ وَكَيْفَ عَرَفْتَ؟
مَا مُحَفِّزُ النَّصْبِ؟ غَرَضٌ أَمْ إِرَادَةٌ أَمْ ضَرُورَةٌ؟
مَاذَا يَكْشِفُ ذٰلِكَ عَنْ حُجَّةِ الكَاتِبِ؟
model: «تَتَعَاوَنَ» مَنْصُوبٌ؛ عَرَفْتُهُ مِنَ الفَتْحَةِ فِي آخِرِهِ.
المُحَفِّزُ «يَتَطَلَّبُ أَنْ»، وَهُوَ إِرَادَةٌ؛ يَكْشِفُ أَنَّ الكَاتِبَ يَرَى التَّعَاوُنَ مَطْلُوبًا لَا مُنْجَزًا.

writing.prompt: Write eighty to ninety words analysing a short built/natural world text of your choice. Identify one subjunctive verb and its trigger (purpose, volition or necessity), explain what it reveals about the writer's argument, and note one indicative verb by contrast.
checklist: One subjunctive verb identified by its fatḥa, with its trigger named.
The trigger classified as purpose, volition or necessity.
What the subjunctive reveals (required / intended / aimed, not yet done).
One indicative verb noted by contrast.
writing.model: يَكْشِفُ النَّصُّ عَنْ حُجَّةِ كَاتِبِهِ مِنْ خِلَالِ صِيَغِ الأَفْعَالِ. فَجُمْلَةُ «يَتَطَلَّبُ الوَضْعُ أَنْ تَتَعَاوَنَ الدُّوَلُ» تَحْمِلُ فِعْلًا مَنْصُوبًا عَرَفْتُهُ مِنَ الفَتْحَةِ، وَمُحَفِّزُهُ «يَتَطَلَّبُ أَنْ»، وَهُوَ مُحَفِّزُ إِرَادَةٍ. وَهٰذَا يَدُلُّ عَلَى أَنَّ الكَاتِبَ يَرَى التَّعَاوُنَ مَطْلُوبًا لَا مُنْجَزًا بَعْدُ. أَمَّا جُمْلَةُ «تَسْتَنْفِدُ المِنْطَقَةُ مِيَاهَهَا» فَفِعْلُهَا مَرْفُوعٌ يَنْتَهِي بِضَمَّةٍ، لِأَنَّهُ يَصِفُ فِعْلًا وَاقِعًا بِلَا مُحَفِّزٍ. لِذٰلِكَ أَقْرَأُ النَّصَّ بِوَعْيٍ بِالصِّيَغِ النَّحْوِيَّةِ، فَهِيَ تَكْشِفُ مَوْقِفَ الكَاتِبِ.

rounds.feedback: The fatḥa after أَنْ marks the subjunctive.

rounds.prompt: Marker: a subjunctive verb ends in …
rounds.feedback: The subjunctive marker is a final fatḥa.
لِكَيْ marks purpose.
يَتَطَلَّبُ أَنْ marks volition.
يَنْبَغِي أَنْ marks necessity.
It marks a required, undone action.
A trigger requires the subjunctive.
With no trigger the verb is indicative.
لِكَيْ requires the subjunctive.
المُضَارِعُ المَنْصُوبُ is the subjunctive present.
يَسْتَنْفِدُ means depletes.

options: name the trigger and read its force
rounds.feedback: R3 needs the trigger named and the force read.
With no trigger the verb is indicative, ending in a ḍamma.

lessons.title: Writing — The Built and Natural World (Paper 4 Extended Writing)
lessons.summary: Write a 145-160 word built/natural-world article that carries all three subjunctive triggers — purpose (لِكَي), volition (يَهْدِفُ أَنْ) and necessity (يَنْبَغِي أَنْ) — for three separate Range marks, alongside both conditionals and the past perfect.
objectives: Plan a four-paragraph environmental article that places each subjunctive trigger explicitly.
Use لِكَي for purpose, a volition verb for intention, and an impersonal expression for necessity.
Integrate both conditional types, the past perfect and reported speech.
Reach 145-160 words with nine or more distinct grammar structures.
success: I use لِكَي + subjunctive to state a purpose.
I use يَهْدِفُ / يَرْجُو / يَخْشَى أَنْ + subjunctive for volition.
I use يَنْبَغِي / يَتَطَلَّبُ / مِنَ الضَّرُورِيِّ أَنْ + subjunctive for necessity.
I keep the final fatḥa on every subjunctive verb and reach 145 words.

teach.title: The three triggers are three separate Range marks
teach.text: For the first time, purpose (لِكَي نَحْمِيَ), volition (يَهْدِفُ المَشْرُوعُ إِلَى أَنْ يُقَلِّلَ) and necessity (يَنْبَغِي أَنْ نَسْتَثْمِرَ) each earn their own Range mark. A P4 essay that uses only one type cannot reach full Range — the balance of all three is what top-grade Arabic looks like.

teach.title: Every subjunctive verb keeps its final fatḥa
teach.text: After any trigger the verb takes a fatḥa: لِكَي نَحْمِيَ, not نَحْمِي; أَنْ يُقَلِّلَ, not يُقَلِّلُ. The ـَ marker is the single highest accuracy criterion in P4, so mark it on every trigger verb before you submit.

grammar.title: Assembling the P4 range with all three triggers
grammar.overview: A synthesis: place a purpose clause, a volition clause and a necessity clause, then weave in both conditionals, the past perfect and reported speech.

rules.heading: Purpose
rules.explanation: A purpose clause states why an action is taken.
examples: نَسْتَثْمِرُ فِي الطَّاقَةِ النَّظِيفَةِ لِكَيْ نَحْمِيَ الأَجْيَالَ القَادِمَةَ

rules.heading: Volition
rules.explanation: A volition verb expresses intention, hope or fear.
examples: يَهْدِفُ المَشْرُوعُ إِلَى أَنْ يُقَلِّلَ الاِنْبِعَاثَاتِ

rules.heading: Necessity
rules.formula: يَنْبَغِي / يَتَطَلَّبُ / مِنَ الضَّرُورِيِّ أَنْ + مَنْصُوبٌ
rules.explanation: An impersonal expression states what must happen.
examples: يَنْبَغِي أَنْ نَسْتَثْمِرَ فِي البُنْيَةِ التَّحْتِيَّةِ
مِنَ الضَّرُورِيِّ أَنْ نُحَافِظَ عَلَى التُّرَاثِ

rules.heading: Conditionals and narrative
rules.formula: إِذَا … سَـ · لَوْ … لَـ · كَانَ قَدْ
rules.explanation: Recommend with a Type 1, reflect with a Type 2, open with a past perfect.
examples: كَانَتِ المَدِينَةُ قَدْ فَقَدَتْ مِسَاحَاتِهَا الخَضْرَاءَ

quiz.prompt: Which clause states a purpose (لِكَي)?
options: نَسْتَثْمِرُ فِي الطَّاقَةِ النَّظِيفَةِ لِكَيْ نَحْمِيَ البِيئَةَ.
quiz.feedback: لِكَي + subjunctive states a purpose.

quiz.prompt: Which clause expresses volition (intention)?
options: يَهْدِفُ المَشْرُوعُ إِلَى أَنْ يُقَلِّلَ الاِنْبِعَاثَاتِ.
quiz.feedback: يَهْدِفُ إِلَى أَنْ expresses intention — a volition trigger.

quiz.prompt: Which clause expresses impersonal necessity?
quiz.feedback: يَنْبَغِي أَنْ is an impersonal necessity trigger.

quiz.prompt: Why do the three triggers matter for Range?
options: Each earns a separate Range mark
One is enough for full Range

listening.title: Listening: an examiner on the three triggers
listening.script: فِي الوَرَقَةِ الرَّابِعَةِ، يَبْلُغُ نَصُّ هٰذِهِ الوَحْدَةِ مِئَةً وَخَمْسًا وَأَرْبَعِينَ إِلَى مِئَةٍ وَسِتِّينَ كَلِمَةً. النِّطَاقُ فِي مُسْتَوَى السَّنَةِ التَّاسِعَةِ يُكَافِئُ المُسَبِّبَاتِ الثَّلَاثَةَ لِلنَّصْبِ بِثَلَاثِ عَلَامَاتٍ مُنْفَصِلَةٍ: عَلَامَةٌ لِلْغَرَضِ مَعَ «لِكَيْ»، وَعَلَامَةٌ لِلْإِرَادَةِ مَعَ «يَهْدِفُ أَوْ يَرْجُو أَوْ يَخْشَى أَنْ»، وَعَلَامَةٌ لِلضَّرُورَةِ مَعَ «يَنْبَغِي أَوْ يَتَطَلَّبُ أَنْ». وَبَعْدَ كُلِّ مُسَبِّبٍ يَأْتِي فِعْلٌ مَنْصُوبٌ بِفَتْحَةٍ فِي آخِرِهِ. النَّصُّ الَّذِي يَحْمِلُ مُسَبِّبًا وَاحِدًا فَقَطْ لَا يَنَالُ النِّطَاقَ الكَامِلَ. اِفْتَحْ بِخَلْفِيَّةٍ فِي المَاضِي التَّامِّ، ثُمَّ أَوْصِ بِشَرْطٍ مِنَ النَّوْعِ الأَوَّلِ، ثُمَّ تَأَمَّلْ بِشَرْطٍ مِنَ النَّوْعِ الثَّانِي، وَاخْتِمْ بِرَابِطٍ رَسْمِيٍّ.

reading.title: Reading: an annotated model (extract)
reading.text: كَانَتْ مُدُنُنَا قَدْ فَقَدَتْ كَثِيرًا مِنْ مِسَاحَاتِهَا الخَضْرَاءِ قَبْلَ أَنْ نَنْتَبِهَ لِلْخَطَرِ. وَاليَوْمَ يَنْبَغِي أَنْ نُعِيدَ التَّوَازُنَ بَيْنَ العُمْرَانِ وَالطَّبِيعَةِ. لِذٰلِكَ أَطْلَقَتِ الحُكُومَةُ مَشْرُوعًا يَهْدِفُ إِلَى أَنْ يَزْرَعَ مَلَايِينَ الأَشْجَارِ، وَنَزْرَعُهَا لِكَيْ نُنَقِّيَ الهَوَاءَ وَنَحْمِيَ الأَجْيَالَ القَادِمَةَ. قَالَ خَبِيرٌ بِيئِيٌّ إِنَّ الاِسْتِدَامَةَ لَيْسَتْ رَفَاهِيَةً بَلْ ضَرُورَةٌ. عَلَاوَةً عَلَى ذٰلِكَ، إِذَا اسْتَثْمَرْنَا فِي الطَّاقَةِ المُتَجَدِّدَةِ، سَنُقَلِّلُ الاِنْبِعَاثَاتِ. وَلَوْ كُنَّا قَدْ بَدَأْنَا مُبَكِّرًا، لَكَانَتْ بِيئَتُنَا أَفْضَلَ حَالًا. وَخِتَامًا، نَرْجُو أَنْ يَتَحَمَّلَ الجَمِيعُ مَسْؤُولِيَّتَهُمْ.

writing.prompt: Write a 145-160 word built/natural-world article. Open with a past-perfect background, then place all three subjunctive triggers — a purpose clause (لِكَي), a volition clause (يَهْدِفُ / يَرْجُو / يَخْشَى أَنْ) and a necessity clause (يَنْبَغِي / يَتَطَلَّبُ أَنْ) — and add a Type 1 recommendation, a Type 2 reflection and a formal connector.
checklist: A past-perfect background opening (كَانَ قَدْ).
All three subjunctive triggers, each with the final fatḥa on its verb.
A Type 1 recommendation and a Type 2 reflection (with the لَـ result).
Reported speech, a formal connector and 145-160 words.

lessons.title: Listening — Built and Natural World Texts
lessons.summary: Complete Paper 1 style academic listening: hear the subjunctive trigger to predict a purpose, a volition or a necessity clause, and tell إِذَا from لَوْ by the result marker.
objectives: Predict which trigger type each question targets before listening.
Distinguish purpose (لِكَي) from volition (يَخْشَى/يَرْجُو أَنْ) and necessity (يَنْبَغِي/يَتَطَلَّبُ أَنْ) by ear.
Focus on the trigger, since the final fatḥa is often reduced in fast speech.
Reach the P4 listening target of fourteen or more out of twenty.
success: I use the trigger to know a subjunctive clause is coming.
I tell a fear (يَخْشَى) from a hope (يَرْجُو) to read attitude.
I hear إِذَا (real) versus لَوْ (hypothetical) by the result marker.
I catch the past perfect and disaster passives in fast speech.

items.note: Focus on this, not the vowel.

teach.title: Hear the trigger, not the final vowel
teach.text: In natural speech the subjunctive fatḥa is fast and often reduced, so do not try to catch it. Instead listen for the trigger: لِكَي tells you a purpose is coming; يَخْشَى / يَرْجُو أَنْ tells you a fear or hope is coming; يَتَطَلَّبُ / يَنْبَغِي أَنْ tells you a requirement is coming. The trigger alone answers the question.

teach.title: Fear and hope are both volition — but opposite attitudes
teach.text: A speaker may say يَخْشَى أَنْ يَتَجَاوَزَ الاِحْتِرَارُ حَدَّهُ (fear), then يَرْجُو أَنْ تُوَقِّعَ الدُّوَلُ الاِتِّفَاقَ (hope). Both are subjunctive volition clauses, but Paper 1 attitude questions depend on telling the fear from the hope.

grammar.title: Hearing subjunctive triggers and conditionals in fast speech

quiz.prompt: You hear لِكَيْ. The clause is …
quiz.feedback: لِكَي signals a purpose clause.

quiz.prompt: You hear يَخْشَى أَنْ. The attitude is …

quiz.prompt: You hear يَرْجُو أَنْ. The attitude is …
quiz.feedback: يَرْجُو signals hope — a volition trigger.

quiz.prompt: Why focus on the trigger, not the final vowel?

quiz.feedback: The final fatḥa is fast and reduced, so the trigger is the reliable signal.

quiz.prompt: You hear a سَـ result. The conditional is …
quiz.feedback: A سَـ result signals a real إِذَا conditional.

quiz.prompt: You hear a لَـ result. The conditional is …
quiz.feedback: A لَـ result signals a counterfactual لَوْ conditional.

quiz.prompt: Which is the past-perfect marker to listen for?
quiz.feedback: كَانَ قَدْ marks the past perfect.

grammar.common_error: Trying to catch the final fatḥa on the subjunctive verb. Since it is reduced in speech, listen for the trigger instead — it tells you the clause type.
grammar.challenge: For three prepared questions, note whether you will listen for a purpose, a volition or a necessity trigger.

mistakes.wrong: سَمِعْتُ «يَنْبَغِي أَنْ» فَظَنَنْتُهُ غَرَضًا.
mistakes.right: سَمِعْتُ «يَنْبَغِي أَنْ» فَعَرَفْتُ أَنَّهُ ضَرُورَةٌ.
mistakes.why: يَنْبَغِي أَنْ signals necessity, not purpose — لِكَي signals purpose.

mistakes.wrong: «يَخْشَى» وَ«يَرْجُو» يَحْمِلَانِ المَوْقِفَ نَفْسَهُ.
mistakes.right: «يَخْشَى» يَحْمِلُ الخَوْفَ وَ«يَرْجُو» يَحْمِلُ الأَمَلَ.
mistakes.why: Both are volition, but يَخْشَى is fear and يَرْجُو is hope.

mistakes.wrong: حَاوَلْتُ الْتِقَاطَ الفَتْحَةِ الأَخِيرَةِ لِأَعْرِفَ النَّصْبَ.

mistakes.why: The final fatḥa is reduced in speech; the trigger is the reliable signal.

listening.title: Listening: an environmental expert on water scarcity
listening.script: يَقُولُ الخَبِيرُ البِيئِيُّ: تُعَانِي المِنْطَقَةُ العَرَبِيَّةُ مِنْ نُدْرَةِ المِيَاهِ بِسَبَبِ قِلَّةِ الأَمْطَارِ وَسُوءِ الإِدَارَةِ. وَتُمَثِّلُ المِيَاهُ المُتَجَدِّدَةُ نِسْبَةً ضَئِيلَةً مِنْ حَاجَتِنَا. يَتَطَلَّبُ الوَضْعُ أَنْ تُخَصِّصَ الحُكُومَاتُ مِيزَانِيَّاتٍ أَكْبَرَ لِلتَّحْلِيَةِ. وَنَخْشَى أَنْ يَتَجَاوَزَ الاِحْتِرَارُ العَالَمِيُّ حُدُودَهُ الآمِنَةَ. إِذَا اعْتَمَدْنَا عَلَى الطَّاقَةِ الشَّمْسِيَّةِ فِي التَّحْلِيَةِ، سَنُخَفِّضُ التَّكَالِيفَ. وَلَوْ كُنَّا قَدِ اسْتَثْمَرْنَا مُبَكِّرًا، لَتَجَنَّبْنَا هٰذِهِ الأَزْمَةَ. وَنَزْرَعُ مَحَاصِيلَ أَقَلَّ اسْتِهْلَاكًا لِلْمَاءِ لِكَيْ نُوَفِّرَ مَوَارِدَنَا. وَأَخِيرًا، نَرْجُو أَنْ تُوَقِّعَ الدُّوَلُ اتِّفَاقًا لِإِدَارَةِ الأَنْهَارِ المُشْتَرَكَةِ.

questions.prompt: What is the main cause of water scarcity?
questions.feedback: نُدْرَةِ المِيَاهِ بِسَبَبِ قِلَّةِ الأَمْطَارِ وَسُوءِ الإِدَارَةِ.

questions.prompt: What does the expert say is required (necessity)?
options: Governments should allocate bigger budgets for desalination
questions.feedback: يَتَطَلَّبُ الوَضْعُ أَنْ تُخَصِّصَ الحُكُومَاتُ مِيزَانِيَّاتٍ أَكْبَرَ لِلتَّحْلِيَةِ.

questions.prompt: What does the expert fear (volition)?
options: That global warming will exceed its safe limits
questions.feedback: نَخْشَى أَنْ يَتَجَاوَزَ الاِحْتِرَارُ العَالَمِيُّ حُدُودَهُ الآمِنَةَ.

questions.prompt: What is the Type 1 recommendation?
options: If they rely on solar power for desalination, costs will fall
questions.feedback: إِذَا اعْتَمَدْنَا عَلَى الطَّاقَةِ الشَّمْسِيَّةِ فِي التَّحْلِيَةِ، سَنُخَفِّضُ التَّكَالِيفَ.

questions.prompt: What is the Type 2 regret?
options: Had they invested earlier, they would have avoided this crisis
questions.feedback: لَوْ كُنَّا قَدِ اسْتَثْمَرْنَا مُبَكِّرًا، لَتَجَنَّبْنَا هٰذِهِ الأَزْمَةَ.

questions.prompt: What purpose is given for low-water crops (لِكَي)?
questions.feedback: نَزْرَعُ مَحَاصِيلَ أَقَلَّ اسْتِهْلَاكًا لِلْمَاءِ لِكَيْ نُوَفِّرَ مَوَارِدَنَا.

questions.prompt: What does the expert hope for (volition)?
options: That states will sign an agreement to manage shared rivers
questions.feedback: نَرْجُو أَنْ تُوَقِّعَ الدُّوَلُ اتِّفَاقًا لِإِدَارَةِ الأَنْهَارِ المُشْتَرَكَةِ.

reading.title: Reading: a listening strategy guide
reading.text: لِتَنْجَحَ فِي الاِسْتِمَاعِ الأَكَادِيمِيِّ، اقْرَأِ الأَسْئِلَةَ أَوَّلًا وَحَدِّدْ نَوْعَ المُسَبِّبِ المَطْلُوبِ. فَإِنْ كَانَ السُّؤَالُ عَنْ غَرَضٍ، فَاسْتَمِعْ إِلَى «لِكَيْ»؛ وَهِيَ وَاضِحَةٌ فِي النُّطْقِ بِمَقْطَعَيْنِ. وَإِنْ كَانَ عَنْ ضَرُورَةٍ، فَاسْتَمِعْ إِلَى «يَتَطَلَّبُ» أَوْ «يَنْبَغِي» قَبْلَ «أَنْ». وَإِنْ كَانَ عَنْ خَوْفٍ أَوْ أَمَلٍ، فَاسْتَمِعْ إِلَى «يَخْشَى» أَوْ «يَرْجُو». أَمَّا الفِعْلُ المَنْصُوبُ نَفْسُهُ فَفَتْحَتُهُ الأَخِيرَةُ كَثِيرًا مَا تُخْتَزَلُ فِي الكَلَامِ السَّرِيعِ، لِذٰلِكَ رَكِّزْ عَلَى المُسَبِّبِ لَا عَلَى الحَرَكَةِ. وَفِي الشَّرْطِ، «سَـ» تَدُلُّ عَلَى شَرْطٍ حَقِيقِيٍّ وَ«لَـ» عَلَى شَرْطٍ افْتِرَاضِيٍّ. وَتَذَكَّرْ أَنَّ الإِجَابَةَ العَامَّةَ كَثِيرًا مَا تَكُونُ مُشَتِّتًا.

questions.prompt: What is the first strategy step?
options: Read the questions and identify the type of trigger needed
questions.feedback: اقْرَأِ الأَسْئِلَةَ أَوَّلًا وَحَدِّدْ نَوْعَ المُسَبِّبِ المَطْلُوبِ.

questions.prompt: How is a purpose question answered by ear?
options: Listen for لِكَي — it is clear in speech
questions.feedback: فَاسْتَمِعْ إِلَى «لِكَيْ»؛ وَهِيَ وَاضِحَةٌ فِي النُّطْقِ.

questions.prompt: Why not rely on catching the final fatḥa?
options: It is often reduced in fast speech
It is louder than the trigger
questions.feedback: فَتْحَتُهُ الأَخِيرَةُ كَثِيرًا مَا تُخْتَزَلُ فِي الكَلَامِ السَّرِيعِ.

questions.prompt: How is a conditional type identified by ear?
options: By the result marker — سَـ real, لَـ hypothetical
questions.feedback: «سَـ» تَدُلُّ عَلَى شَرْطٍ حَقِيقِيٍّ وَ«لَـ» عَلَى شَرْطٍ افْتِرَاضِيٍّ.

questions.prompt: What is often a distractor?
questions.feedback: الإِجَابَةَ العَامَّةَ كَثِيرًا مَا تَكُونُ مُشَتِّتًا.

prompts: مَا الغَرَضُ الَّذِي سَمِعْتَهُ؟ وَبِأَيِّ مُسَبِّبٍ عَرَفْتَهُ؟
مَا الضَّرُورَةُ الَّتِي سَمِعْتَهَا؟ وَبِأَيِّ مُسَبِّبٍ؟
هَلْ سَمِعْتَ خَوْفًا أَمْ أَمَلًا؟ وَكَيْفَ مَيَّزْتَ بَيْنَهُمَا؟
model: سَمِعْتُ «يَتَطَلَّبُ الوَضْعُ أَنْ تُخَصِّصَ الحُكُومَاتُ مِيزَانِيَّاتٍ»، وَعَرَفْتُهَا مِنْ «يَتَطَلَّبُ».
نَعَمْ، «نَخْشَى أَنْ يَتَجَاوَزَ الاِحْتِرَارُ حَدَّهُ» خَوْفٌ، وَ«نَرْجُو أَنْ تُوَقِّعَ الدُّوَلُ» أَمَلٌ.

lessons.title: Consolidation — Speaking Preparation and Full Subjunctive Mastery
lessons.arabic: تَرْسِيخُ الوَحْدَةِ — إِعْدَادُ التَّحَدُّثِ وَإِتْقَانُ المُضَارِعِ المَنْصُوبِ
lessons.summary: Master the P4 error zones and use all three subjunctive triggers spontaneously in a built/natural-world topic conversation, with both conditional types and the past perfect secure across all four skills.
objectives: Correct the twelve most common P4 errors, led by the subjunctive fatḥa.
Retrieve all three subjunctive triggers, both conditionals and the past perfect accurately.
Use لِكَي, a volition verb and يَتَطَلَّبُ أَنْ spontaneously in speech.
Prepare five topic-conversation answers to assessment standard.
success: I keep the final fatḥa on every subjunctive verb after a trigger.
I keep the لَـ prefix in every Type 2 result and a past verb after لَوْ.
I answer the لَوْ question with a Type 2 and the يَتَطَلَّبُ question with a subjunctive.
I use لِكَي for purpose unprompted when a question asks why.

teach.title: The three highest-frequency P4 slips
teach.text: First, dropping the subjunctive fatḥa: لِكَي نَحْمِي should be لِكَي نَحْمِيَ, and أَنْ نَسْتَثْمِرُ should be أَنْ نَسْتَثْمِرَ. Second, a Type 2 result without the لَـ: لَوْ بَدَأْنَا، نَجَحْنَا should be لَوْ بَدَأْنَا، لَنَجَحْنَا. Third, a broken passive: يُدَمَّرَتْ should be دُمِّرَتْ.

teach.title: Answer each question with the trigger it invites
teach.text: A why question invites لِكَي (لِكَي نَحْمِيَ …). A يَتَطَلَّبُ question invites a necessity subjunctive (يَتَطَلَّبُ الأَمْرُ أَنْ نُخَصِّصَ …). A لَوْ question invites a Type 2 (لَوْ كَانَ لَدَيَّ … لَـ …). Matching the answer to the trigger is what earns the quality-of-language mark.

grammar.title: Repairing the P4 error zones
grammar.overview: Targeted error correction across the spine: the subjunctive fatḥa after every trigger, the Type 2 لَـ result, the past verb after لَوْ, and the disaster passives.

rules.heading: Subjunctive after a trigger
rules.explanation: Every subjunctive verb keeps its final fatḥa.

rules.heading: Type 2 result
rules.explanation: The result verb carries a لَـ prefix.

rules.heading: Past verb after لَوْ
rules.explanation: لَوْ is followed by a past-tense verb.

rules.heading: Disaster passive
rules.explanation: The passive of a reported disaster is fixed in shape.

listening.title: Listening: a mock environmental-conference conversation
listening.script: المُعَلِّمُ: صِفْ نِظَامًا بِيئِيًّا فِي العَالَمِ العَرَبِيِّ تُعْجَبُ بِهِ. الطَّالِبُ: يُعْجِبُنِي نَهْرُ النِّيلِ لِأَنَّهُ يَضُمُّ تَنَوُّعًا كَبِيرًا، وَكَانَتِ الحَضَارَاتُ قَدْ نَشَأَتْ عَلَى ضِفَافِهِ. المُعَلِّمُ: مَا الَّذِي يَتَطَلَّبُهُ الحِفَاظُ عَلَيْهِ؟ الطَّالِبُ: يَتَطَلَّبُ الأَمْرُ أَنْ نُخَصِّصَ مِيزَانِيَّاتٍ أَكْبَرَ وَأَنْ نَحُدَّ مِنَ التَّلَوُّثِ. المُعَلِّمُ: وَلِمَاذَا نَفْعَلُ ذٰلِكَ؟ الطَّالِبُ: نَفْعَلُهُ لِكَيْ نَصُونَ المَوْرِدَ لِلْأَجْيَالِ القَادِمَةِ. المُعَلِّمُ: لَوْ كَانَتْ لَدَيْكَ صَلَاحِيَّاتُ وَزِيرِ البِيئَةِ، مَاذَا كُنْتَ سَتُغَيِّرُ؟ الطَّالِبُ: لَوْ كَانَتْ لَدَيَّ صَلَاحِيَّاتُهُ، لَأَطْلَقْتُ مَشْرُوعًا وَطَنِيًّا لِتَحْلِيَةِ المِيَاهِ. المُعَلِّمُ: أَجْوِبَةٌ مُتَوَازِنَةٌ اسْتَعْمَلْتَ فِيهَا المُسَبِّبَاتِ الثَّلَاثَةَ تِلْقَائِيًّا.

reading.title: Reading: twelve sentences to repair
reading.text: تَحْتَوِي هٰذِهِ القَائِمَةُ عَلَى أَخْطَاءٍ شَائِعَةٍ فِي السَّنَةِ التَّاسِعَةِ. الأَوَّلُ فِي النَّصْبِ بَعْدَ لِكَيْ: «نَزْرَعُ الأَشْجَارَ لِكَيْ نَحْمِي البِيئَةَ» — وَالصَّوَابُ «نَحْمِيَ». الثَّانِي فِي النَّصْبِ بَعْدَ أَنْ: «يَنْبَغِي أَنْ نَسْتَثْمِرُ» — وَالصَّوَابُ «نَسْتَثْمِرَ». الثَّالِثُ فِي جَوَابِ لَوْ: «لَوْ بَدَأْنَا مُبَكِّرًا، نَجَحْنَا» — وَالصَّوَابُ «لَنَجَحْنَا». الرَّابِعُ فِي زَمَنِ فِعْلِ لَوْ: «لَوْ نَسْتَثْمِرُ» — وَالصَّوَابُ «لَوِ اسْتَثْمَرْنَا». الخَامِسُ فِي الفِعْلِ المَبْنِيِّ لِلْمَجْهُولِ: «يُدَمَّرَتِ المَبَانِي» — وَالصَّوَابُ «دُمِّرَتْ». وَالدَّرْسُ المُشْتَرَكُ أَنَّ لِكُلِّ بِنْيَةٍ عَلَامَةً دَقِيقَةً يَجِبُ ضَبْطُهَا.

مَا الَّذِي يَتَطَلَّبُهُ الحِفَاظُ عَلَى التُّرَاثِ المَعْمَارِيِّ فِي رَأْيِكَ؟

writing.prompt: Write eighty to ninety words preparing for the P4 topic conversation. Answer two of the assessment questions, using all three subjunctive triggers, a Type 2 conditional and the past perfect, with every marker accurate.
checklist: A past perfect (كَانَ قَدْ …) with correct agreement.
A purpose clause (لِكَي), a necessity clause (يَتَطَلَّبُ / يَنْبَغِي أَنْ) and a volition clause.
A Type 2 conditional with the لَـ result.

writing.model: كَانَتْ مُدُنُنَا قَدْ فَقَدَتْ كَثِيرًا مِنْ تُرَاثِهَا العُمْرَانِيِّ قَبْلَ أَنْ نَنْتَبِهَ لِقِيمَتِهِ. وَأَرَى أَنَّ الحِفَاظَ عَلَيْهِ يَتَطَلَّبُ أَنْ نُخَصِّصَ مِيزَانِيَّاتٍ لِلتَّرْمِيمِ وَأَنْ نَحُدَّ مِنَ الإِهْمَالِ. وَنَفْعَلُ ذٰلِكَ لِكَيْ نَصُونَ هُوِيَّتَنَا وَنَحْمِيَ ذَاكِرَتَنَا الجَمَاعِيَّةَ. وَنَرْجُو أَنْ تَتَغَيَّرَ نَظْرَةُ النَّاسِ إِلَى المَبَانِي القَدِيمَةِ. وَلَوْ كَانَتْ لَدَيَّ صَلَاحِيَّاتُ وَزِيرِ البِيئَةِ، لَأَطْلَقْتُ حَمْلَةً وَطَنِيَّةً لِلتَّشْجِيرِ وَلَدَعَمْتُ الطَّاقَةَ المُتَجَدِّدَةَ. فَهٰذِهِ الخُطُوَاتُ تَجْمَعُ بَيْنَ حِمَايَةِ الطَّبِيعَةِ وَصَوْنِ العُمْرَانِ مَعًا.

rounds.prompt: Necessity: complete — يَنْبَغِي أَنْ ___ فِي الطَّاقَةِ المُتَجَدِّدَةِ.
rounds.feedback: After أَنْ the verb is subjunctive: نَسْتَثْمِرَ.
After أَنْ the verb is subjunctive: تَنْجَحَ.

rounds.prompt: Type 2: complete — لَوْ بَدَأْنَا مُبَكِّرًا، ___ فِي الحِمَايَةِ.
rounds.feedback: A Type 2 result takes the لَـ prefix.

rounds.prompt: Verb after لَوْ: complete — لَوِ ___ مُبَكِّرًا، لَتَجَنَّبْنَا الأَزْمَةَ.
rounds.feedback: لَوْ is followed by a past-tense verb.
The past passive is دُمِّرَتْ.
أُعْلِنَتْ is the past passive “was declared”.

rounds.prompt: Preposition: complete — يَهْدِفُ المَشْرُوعُ ___ أَنْ يُقَلِّلَ الاِنْبِعَاثَاتِ.
rounds.feedback: يَهْدِفُ is fixed with إِلَى before أَنْ.
After أَنْ the verb must be subjunctive: نُحَافِظَ.
A Type 2 result cannot drop the لَـ.
التِّلْقَائِيَّةُ is spontaneity.

rounds.prompt: Spontaneity: which answers the why question with a purpose?
rounds.feedback: A why question is answered with a لِكَي purpose clause.

rounds.prompt: Report: complete — قَالَ الخَبِيرُ ___ الاِسْتِدَامَةَ ضَرُورَةٌ.
rounds.feedback: قَالَ takes إِنَّ.

rounds.prompt: Transfer: which answer is the most complete and accurate?
options: كَانَتْ مَدِينَتِي قَدْ فَقَدَتْ حَدَائِقَهَا، وَيَتَطَلَّبُ الأَمْرُ أَنْ نُخَصِّصَ مِيزَانِيَّةً لِكَيْ نَصُونَ الطَّبِيعَةَ.
rounds.feedback: A past perfect, a necessity trigger and a purpose clause together.

live_builder.target: Build an assessment answer from a past-perfect background, a necessity clause and a purpose clause.
groups: كَانَتْ مَدِينَتِي قَدْ فَقَدَتْ حَدَائِقَهَا قَبْلَ أَنْ نَنْتَبِهَ لِقِيمَتِهَا
كَانَتِ الحَضَارَاتُ قَدْ نَشَأَتْ عَلَى ضِفَافِ النَّهْرِ
كُنَّا قَدْ أَهْمَلْنَا التُّرَاثَ العُمْرَانِيَّ لِسَنَوَاتٍ
وَيَتَطَلَّبُ الحِفَاظُ عَلَيْهِ أَنْ نُخَصِّصَ مِيزَانِيَّاتٍ لِلتَّرْمِيمِ
وَيَنْبَغِي أَنْ نَحُدَّ مِنَ التَّلَوُّثِ وَالإِهْمَالِ
وَمِنَ الضَّرُورِيِّ أَنْ نَسْتَثْمِرَ فِي الطَّاقَةِ المُتَجَدِّدَةِ
وَنَفْعَلُ ذٰلِكَ لِكَيْ نَصُونَ هُوِيَّتَنَا لِلْأَجْيَالِ القَادِمَةِ
وَنَعْمَلُ عَلَيْهِ لِكَيْ نَحْمِيَ ذَاكِرَتَنَا الجَمَاعِيَّةَ
وَنُطَوِّرُهُ لِكَيْ نُوَازِنَ بَيْنَ العُمْرَانِ وَالطَّبِيعَةِ
live_builder.feedback: Each background, necessity clause and purpose clause is accurate on its own, so any three different combinations work.
